entities.summary: Jörg Breu the Elder, a prominent painter of the German Danube school, played a significant role in the artistic development of Augsburg during the 16th century. Born in Augsburg, Germany, around 1480, Breu the Elder was the son of a weaver and received his artistic training from his father. He was a key figure in the Augsburg workshop of Daniel Hopfer, where he developed his unique style and became known for his intricate woodcuts and engravings. Breu the Elder's work had a lasting impact on the region, influencing generations of artists and contributing to the city's rich cultural heritage. His legacy can still be seen in the many museums and galleries that showcase his works, including the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister in Dresden. As a master of his craft, Breu the Elder's contributions to the artistic world are a testament to his skill and dedication. Through his work, he helped to establish Augsburg as a major center for artistic innovation, leaving a lasting mark on the city's cultural identity.

entities.summary:
Jörg Breu the Elder, a painter of the German Danube school, was born in Augsburg, Germany in 1475 and died in 1537. He was the son of a weaver and trained as an artist in his father's workshop.

Breu's most notable work is the 'Nativity with the Christ Child', a painting that showcases his mastery of the Danube school style. The painting features a dramatic and emotive depiction of the birth of Jesus, with intricate details and a sense of movement.

Breu's legacy can be seen in the many artists who followed in his footsteps, including his own son, Jörg Breu the Younger. The 'Nativity with the Christ Child' remains one of the most celebrated works of the German Danube school, and Breu's innovative style continues to inspire artists to this day.
